svg.text: ADR-0009 — the whole runtime lives in a supervised hyprlayer-server process. The desktop is always a client: locally over a socket, remotely over SSH.
Hyprlayer.app — holds no runtime of its own
most of them one RPC call
connect · spawn · evict a stale server
on the host, over ssh + curl
which server to reach — decided locally,
because there is no server to ask yet
a newer client evicts an older server
hyprlayer-server — one runtime, one profile, no per-connection identity
accept loop — one task tree per connection, aborted on stop
a reader task · a writer task — the only writer to the socket
one task per request · a StreamRegistry of abort handles
one subscription to the runtime's broadcast, fanned out to every client
one runtime per app_data_dir — one settings.json, one hyprlayer.db, one session set
cargo rejects the cycle, so the direction needs no other rule
What the server owns, on its own machine
everything the desktop used to touch directly
A daemonised server has no SSH_AUTH_SOCK, so every attach sends one and
the server merges it at each child spawn. Last attach wins — except
opencode serve, which bakes it in and keeps the first.
Version skew is eviction, not negotiation
A newer client asks an older server to shut down, waits for the profile
lock, and spawns its own — which ends every live session on that
A failed connect still opens the window
Into a recovery state that retries. The one exception is
runtime_in_use: another Hyprlayer holds the lock, which is
single-instance's job, and that arm still exits.
